# mabinogi-013 — review

## Pass 1 (2026-11-15)

I checked all 141 units: each note label against its form, `t` → `l` word by word, `l` ↔ `i`, the house renderings,
consistency with 001/011/012, and whether every establishment-log item appears in a note. I read the Red Book
(Rhŷs & Evans 1905, djvu text ll. 2655–2850) for the whole part. I viewed the Evans image for col. 99 ll. 14–28
(llẏ6 y 6eil-|gi gan pob: both certain). I did not consult any modern English translation. Every edit was made by
script, and no `t` was touched (asserted). The count is still 141, and no `p` fields were added.

### Changes

- 20 · n · major · ys bychan a beth was explained as "a for o 'of a thing'; the construction is not certain".
  It is the a beth idiom that the published first part already glosses (001: ys glut a beth, ys iawn a beth), and
  the Red Book has the same words · note rewritten to "it is a small thing", with the 001 parallel. uyd softened
  after the relative a.
- 16, 54 · l · minor · Duw a ro da it was given as 'God it-is-that may-give'. 011 has 'God may-he-give good
  to-you', and the house table has 'God may-he-repay' · changed to the 011 form.
- 104 · l · minor · Duw a dalho ywch was given as 'God it-is-that may-repay', against the house rendering 'God
  may-he-repay to-you' · changed to the house form.
- 24 · i · minor · Dygaf y Duw uyg kyffes was rendered "I swear to God by my confession". 011 (unit 109) has the
  same oath as "I make my confession to God", and the house rule says a repeated formula gets the same English ·
  i changed to "I make my confession to God"; the note now points to 011.
- 23 · l · minor · 'until he-gets-it from me': no 'it' is in the Welsh (yny caffo y genhyf i) · '-it' removed.
- 83 · l · minor · l had 'Glamorgan', against the rule that names take the modern Welsh form (i already has
  Morgannwg) · changed to 'Morgannwg'.
- 66 · n · minor · yn wimon was said to be "softened after yn" without saying which yn. The preposition 'in'
  would give the nasal mutation · note now names the predicative yn ('becoming, as').
- 3 · n · minor · "llen is feminine, but ll is not written softened after the article" made it a spelling matter.
  ll (like rh) does not soften after the feminine article · reworded.
- 92 · n · minor · Hir bylgeint: the softening was put down to "an adverb of time". The cause is hir, an
  adjective standing before its noun · corrected.
- 91 · n · minor · a gweirwyt: the softening was not named (g is the softened k of kyweirwyt) · added; the note
  also gives the Red Book's a gyweirwyt.
- 90 · n · minor · "as Ynteu e hun Wydyon in col. 95": that sentence is in col. 94 (col. 95 l. 1 is yn
  gyuareisket, unit 12) · corrected; added the 011 parallel Ynteu Wydyon.
- 100 · n · minor · (llyw, gan pob: uncertain readings) The note said the reading "is not certain". On the image
  llẏ6 is certain, and the Red Book has lliw and gan bop · note now says the letters are certain, the reading is
  kept, and it is read as lliw, with the Red Book forms given; welet's softening named (object of chawn).
- 72 · n · minor · gwiscof was called "1 sg. present subjunctive" with no word on the odd ending · added -of
  beside -wyf (the Red Book has gwisgwyf, also unsoftened after yny).
- 72, 76, 89 · n · minor · the establishment log's "!"-like line-end marks (col. 97 l. 27, col. 98 ll. 4 and 29)
  were not in any note, though 010/011 state such marks · stated.
- 75 · n · minor · the "/" after pob (col. 97, last line) was not stated · stated.
- 128 · n · minor · the stray "'" before arueu (col. 100 l. 25) was not stated · stated.
- 133 · n · minor · the suspension stroke over y gyt (col. 101 l. 2) was not stated · stated.
- 25 · n · minor · (yr hwnn yd wyt ti) The Red Book's yn uorwyn, which supports the note's "y for yn", was not
  given, and the other way to read yr was left out · added the Red Book reading. Also added yr as the preposition
  'for, in spite of' (as in yr hynny), offered as an alternative.
- 29 · n · minor · degach was called softened with no cause given, after the masculine lledyr · cause and
  irregularity stated.
- 71 · i, n · minor · (bryt / furyf) i had "let the boy go back into their true looks". 'their' after a singular
  noun misleads the English reader · i "let the boy go back to his own looks". l keeps 'their form', and the note
  now adds that y may be 'his' with the softening not written. It also says that the Red Book has the same
  unsoftened yny b[r]yt ehun and lacks the furyf clause.
- 124 · i · style · "many a mother's son": 'mother's' is not in the Welsh (llawer mab) and sounds borrowed ·
  "many a son".
- 80 · i · style · "took the coast road up": there is no road in the Welsh (yr aruordir y uynyd) · "went up along
  the coastland".
- 42 · i · style · "And there: the shoes were too big" was awkward. 011 renders nachaf as "see" · "And see, the
  shoes were too big."
- 33 · l · style · 'one-might-not-recognise-them': the object is not in the Welsh · '-them' dropped.
- 81 · n · style · (y Geuyn) the note did not say why y is not the article · added: keuyn is masculine and would
  not soften after it.
- 7 · n · style · (hof) added that the Red Book has hoff both times.
- 12, 126 · n · style · uot ← bot: the cause of the softening was not named · named.
- 94 · n · style · yn gynghan: the softening was not named · added.
- 112 · n · style · (yn gwbyl) added that the Red Book also has it unsoftened.
- 19 · n · style · (ba doi) added that the Red Book has the same, pa doi.
- 61 · n · style · (y Lleu ef) added that ef could repeat the subject, and that the Red Book has the same words.

Counts: 1 major, 22 minor, 12 style, counted per unit (16/54, 72/76/89 and 12/126 each count once per unit).

### Refused

- 0, 94 (Wydyon, gyniweir softened after oed): Middle Welsh often softens a subject straight after a form of bot.
  The Red Book also has yd oed wydyon. Kept.
- 9 (Ynteu e hun Wydyon): softening in apposition after the pronoun, the same call as 011's Ynteu Wydyon. Kept.
- 81 (y Geuyn): the call that y is the preposition is right. Only the wording was expanded (above).
- 112 (yn gwbyl unsoftened): stated as written. Kept.
- 72 (gwiscof unsoftened after yny): the call is right. Only the ending was added (above).
- 100 (gan pob): confirmed on the image. Kept.
- 124 (eneit 'life'): 011 has eneit only as the vocative 'soul'/'friend' (units 15, 20), and that is no
  precedent for colli y eneit. 'Lose his life' is the plain sense, and the note gives both meanings. Kept.
- 12 (yn gyuareisket), 28 (morwyal), 76 (dihirwch), 128 (yn luttaf), 133 (ossymdeithawc), 120 (heb with no
  subject), 129 (inheu), 102 (wnawn i): each is hedged or stated plainly in its note, in line with the log. Kept.
- 73 (handid o'th direidi di): the hedge and the free i are acceptable; the Red Book has the same words. Kept.
- 24 (dygaf, "or perhaps a form of tyngu"): the alternative is a real view about the oath formula, and the note
  is hedged. Kept, with the 011 cross-reference.
- 77, 83, 98, 119 (vocatives 'O lad', 'O porter' …): 011 has "Lad" for A was, but 001/012 have 'O …'
  ('O chieftain', 'O men', 'O maiden'). The draft follows the majority practice. Kept.
- 28/29 (morwyal 'sea-wrack' beside guimon 'wrack'): the article in o'r guimon shows the same weed is meant.
  The overlap in English is acceptable. Kept.
- 109 i "with the maidens' help" for ui a'r morynyon: this reads the 1 sg. verb with its joint subject as the
  sense needs. Kept.
- Names (Lleu Llaw Gyffes, Blodeuedd, Dinas Dinlle, Aber Menai, Bryn Arien, Cefn Clydno, Morgannwg, Dunoding,
  Eifionydd, Mur Castell): the modern Welsh forms are right, and the notes say how the manuscript spellings differ
  (Llew/Lleu, Blodeued, Dinllef, Menei, Aryen, Clutno, Dinodig, Eiwynyd). Kept. The l of 65 keeps the name's
  meaning 'Lleu Hand Steady' at the naming. Kept.
